intro1:
A kaleidoscope has an infinite number of colours: reds. Blues. Yellows. Greens.
Warm. Bright. Vivid. Soothing. Sometimes the colours blend together. Much like the way people interact with one another.
There is love, kindness, understanding, politeness, compassion. Or, conversely: rudeness, lies, hatred, polemics, persecution, violence.
intro2: Together with pupils from the Europa-Gymnasium Frankfurt (Oder), the music school and the Frankfurt (Oder) Singing Academy, as well as the Lyzeum at Collegium Polonicum in Słubice, we aim to explore and discuss the themes in this project based on the historical story of Jesus of Nazareth. We will do so with the help of music by Johann Sebastian Bach from his two famous Passions: the St Matthew Passion and the St John Passion. We will also feature pieces by the Argentine pioneer of the ‘tango nuevo’, Astor Piazzolla – for example, from his opera ‘Maria de Buenos Aires’. Our new Chief Conductor, Felix Mildenberger, will be in charge of the musical direction.
intro3: Are the colours of our relationships always clear-cut? Do they blend together? What comes of it? How does this affect our relationship? How can we live together harmoniously?
intro4: We want to explore all these questions artistically with the German and Polish pupils: through choreography, film, singing, acting and drawing.
closing: What will come of it? A riot of colours, we hope. Just like a kaleidoscope. And perhaps also – insights.
termin1: Sat 10 Oct 2026 · 3.00 pm & 4.45 pm — Town Hall Atrium, Frankfurt (Oder)
musik_intro: Johann Sebastian Bach and Astor Piazzolla. Why, of all people, have we chosen music by these two seemingly contrasting composers from completely different eras and cultural backgrounds? Why do we believe that their music expresses particularly well what we want to convey to young people? Perhaps because their music is almost pictorially predestined to express the themes we have chosen. Perhaps because Piazzolla developed a passion not only for tango at an early age, but even earlier for the great Baroque composer Bach.
musik_intro2: Or perhaps quite simply because Martin Luther’s words apply to their music:
luther_zitat: “Music is a pure gift and a blessing from God; it drives away the devil, it makes people happy, and through it one forgets all one’s vices.”
mitmachen: As a member of Förderverein, you are helping to make projects such as Kaleidoskop possible – and enabling children and young people from Frankfurt (Oder) and Słubice to bring music, theatre and big questions to the stage together.
